93118.overview:
The Addams Family is a pinball game designed by Pat Lawlor, illustrated by John Youssi, and released in 1992 by Williams Electronics (under the Bally label). It is based on the 1991 film of the same name, and Raúl Juliá and Anjelica Huston reprised their roles as Gomez and Morticia, respectively.

The game casts you as a visitor exploring the Addams' mansion, and the most obvious objective is survival. Not that it's easy, with the swamp and the graveyard out back, the electric chair in the parlor, the living bear carpet, secret passageways, and the Mamushka. While Gomez and Morticia try to be supportive, Thing is ready to lend a hand by helping you work the flippers. If you can get through all 12 rooms (game modes and awards), you'll have a chance to Tour The Mansion.

The Addams Family was the first game to have a series of modes which are played before a wizard mode. Almost all subsequently released pinball machines included a wizard mode.

The Addams Family ultimately became the best-selling pinball game ever, breaking all previous sales records with 20,270 units sold. Bally eventually re-released it in 1994 as The Addams Family: Special Collector's Edition, with gold elements on the cabinets, more quotes in the game, and an expanded set of rules.

177758.overview:
Apollo 13 is a 1995 pinball game designed by Joe Balcer and Joe Kaminkow, based on the film of the same name. Kevin Bacon (Jack Swigert), Bill Paxton (Fred Haise), and Gary Sinise (Ken Mattingly) provided custom speech for this game. The game is notable for its 13-ball multiball mode, the most of any pinball machine.

This is a very dense pinball table; playfield toys include an elevating Saturn V rocket, a lunar LEM module, a countdown LED, and a rotating Moon. Collect orbits around the table to Advance the Spacecraft around the Moon and return to Earth, and perform various Apollo Missions along the way — perform a manual burn to straighten the orbiter, fix the Life Support systems, fix the CO2 scrubbers, and take care of the Master Alarm. For more points, shoot the Saturn and load up for multiball, or use gravitynote  to slingshot pinballs over the Moon. 

Even with all these features, the biggest appeal of the game is its 13 Ball Blastoff Multiball, where thirteen balls are unloaded onto the playfield. Up to six people can play at once, either individually or in teams, and the game offers "Novice" and "Wizard" difficulty settings for players. Approximately 2,000 units of Apollo 13 were produced by Sega Pinball.

181299.overview:
The Aaron Spelling pinball machine is one of the rarest and most exclusive pinball machines ever created. Produced by Data East in February 1992, it was never intended for public sale. 

The machine was commissioned by Spelling's wife, Candy Spelling, as a personalized gift for his birthday, and only 3 units were ever manufactured. Reports suggest the commissioning cost was approximately $170,000. 

It is a modified version of the Lethal Weapon 3 table. The backglass and playfield feature various TV shows produced by Spelling, including Dynasty, Charlie's Angels, The Love Boat, and Beverly Hills, 90210.

183988.overview:
Apache!, released in 1978, is a pinball machine from Taito do Brasil. The playfield layout is identical to Gottlieb's 1975 table Fast Draw.

It is notable for its transition-era technology, as it uses TTL (Transistor-Transistor Logic) technology, which sits between traditional electromechanical systems and later fully digital Solid State (SS) systems.

192412.overview:
Aliens Legacy (or Aliens Pinball Legacy) is a highly regarded original pinball table for the Future Pinball platform based on the sci-fi horror and action franchise "Alien". Originally designed in 2010 by David Eisner (aka Pinballwzd), the table has since received many significant updates by the community, most notably by SLAMT1LT and TerryRed.

During game play, you will try to avoid being overcome by approaching Aliens as seen on the Motion Tracker. The only way to prevent the approaching swarm is to shoot the aliens in the pop bumper area. If the aliens get to the bottom right of the tracker, all flippers will be lost and your ball will be over.

When the Aliens get half-way down the tracker, the Power Failure Lamp will be Lit. This is only a temporary action. Hitting the Power target will restore power if the aliens are pushed back past half-way. The only way to prevent power failure is to keep the aliens back to the outer perimeter.

The object of the game is to work through the game modes in order until you get to the final Nuke Site mode. By completing this mode, you will arm the nuke and escape via the POD ship. A flashing green light indicates a mode is ready; a flashing red light indicates the mode is active.

BUG HUNT:
------------

To start this mode, shoot the ball into the left drop hole on the POD mini-playfield. Starting a mode scores 5,000 points. Dropping through a hole when NOT starting a mode scores 250 points. Complete the E-G-G-S drop targets. Kill 20 Aliens in the pop bumpers "Egg Nest".

SAVE NEWT:
------------

To start this mode, shoot the ball into the right drop hole "Save Newt" on the POD mini-playfield. Hit the Open Nest target under the right POD hole.  This will open the diverter above the pop bumpers. You must enter the pop bumper area through the open diverter within 15 seconds. If time expires, the diverter will close and you'll have to hit the Open Nest target again. Making the shot to the pop bumpers through the diverter awards 10,000 points. Each Pop Bumper will be flashing and will award Double Pop Bumper Scores for a maximum of 60 seconds. At any time AFTER the diverter entrance has been made, hit the Elevator to complete the mode. 

NUKE SITE:
------------

To start this mode, shoot the ball into the middle drop hole on the POD mini-playfield. A random code is made up of the (1 - 2 - 3 - 4) targets.  The targets around the playfield will have to be hit in order. Each correctly hit target scores 1,000 points. Once the code is entered, hit the POD door to confirm the code. After confirmation, you have 30 seconds to shoot for the Elevator and drop the ball into the center hole. Completing this mode scores 250,000.  If the shots are not made in the allotted time, the player will lose the ball.

ALIEN LEGACY:
----------------

The fourth mode of this game is 3-ball multiball. Locking a ball awards 10,000 Points.

195805.overview: Amazon Hunt is a pinball machine released by D. Gottlieb & Co. in September 1983. It has a jungle adventure theme with two flippers, no ramps, and no multiball. Designed by Ed Krynski with artwork by Larry Day, it is part of the Gottlieb System 80A series and had a production run of 1,515 units.

208964.overview:
American Dad! is one of four tables in the Balls of Glory table pack, based on animated Fox TV sitcoms. Released in the fall of 2015 for Zen Pinball 2 and Pinball FX 2 (and released for Pinball FX 3 in 2017), the table depicts the many odd adventures of an American upper-class family headed by CIA agent Stan Smith. 

The goal of this table is to complete eight different missions that depict iconic moments from the American Dad! television series, with each mission spotting a letter in the word AMERICAN; once AMERICAN is fully spelled, May the Best Stan Win wizard mode will be qualified at the mission sinkhole. The first time through the missions, AMERICAN letters can simply be collected by starting a mission; on further attempts, they have to be completed by making the required shots without losing the ball.

To start a mission, the player can destroy Klaus' fishbowl with three hits to reveal the mission hole, then shoot the ball into it. The mission that will start is the one shown on a small television screen near the left ramp, and can be changed to the next episode in the listed sequence below by shooting the mini-orbit during normal play. The mission timers, shot requirements, and score rewards are tied to the current threat level. 

Tips:

Shooting the loops on the Stan Smith Residence mini-playfield is a very easy way to get a high score. Each loop shot scores more points than the previous with no limit, and it is very possible to get 200 million points on a single visit with a low threat level.

The side ramp is one of the most important shots in the game, as shooting it after spelling COP is integral to lighting the outlane kickbacks. Shooting the Cop mini-orbit is the easiest way to reliably shoot for the side ramp, though with practice, the right orbit feeds the upper flipper nicely as well.

The Roger targets and Klaus' fishbowl can bounce the ball sharply towards the outhole or outlanes, without a ball saver in sight; always try to have the kickbacks active to avoid these drains. Shots to the center mini-loop occasionally bounce down the outlanes, but the game will automatically save these balls.

208966.overview:
Archer is one of four tables in the Balls of Glory table pack, based on animated Fox TV sitcoms. Released in the fall of 2015 and available for Zen Pinball 2, Pinball FX 2 and Pinball FX 3, this table is based on the many exploits of the agents of the International Secret Intelligence Service, including the well-known agent Sterling Archer.

The goal of this table is to help Archer achieve awesomeness through the completion of many missions. The amount of awesomeness gained depends on the difficulty of the mission and the awesomeness multiplier's current level. Each mission has its own unique activation method and must be completed without losing the ball. Missions can be repeated and completed as many times as possible until enough awesomeness is earned to start the Awesomeness Multiball. 

Tips:

You have complete freedom on which missions you want to complete to earn enough awesomeness, so take advantage of that to only go for the mission sets that you’re comfortable with playing. Remember that the missions from the bumpers and the Woodhouse missions tend to score far less awesomeness than the other sets; it might be better to ignore these unless you’re close to starting them.

Be strategic with acquiring armory perks! Raise lots of funds, then once you have a lot, carefully spell out SPY on the target posts to unlock the armory at the right ramp. Crucial perks to buy there are the awesomeness multipliers, permanent ball save, and extra ball. If you’re worried that the SPY targets will cause drains, try completing them during the ball save timer at the beginning of a new ball.

Malory Multiball is generally not worth the risk of going for, as hilarious as the prank voicemails are; CB Multiball is a little easier to activate but still doesn’t score much. Avalanche Multiball is where the big points are and should be prioritized over the other two Multiball modes at all times if you’re looking to get a high score.

208974.overview: Avengers: Age of Ultron is one of the three Marvel pinball tables available in the Cinematic Pack for Pinball FX 3, originally released as a standalone table for Pinball FX 2 and Zen Pinball 2 shortly before the film's release. The table depicts the events of the 2015 MCU film of the same name, following the Avengers' efforts to stop a rogue AI originally created by Tony Stark to defend the world.

208977.overview: Ant-Man is one of the three Marvel pinball tables that are part of the Cinematic Pack, released in 2015 and available for Zen Pinball 2, Pinball FX 2 and Pinball FX 3. Based on the 2015 Marvel Cinematic Universe film Ant-Man, directed by Peyton Reed, this pinball table explores the efforts of scientist Hank Pym to recruit the crook Scott Lang to become the superhero Ant-Man and use his size-altering powers to stage a daring heist of the Yellowjacket, a weaponized, shrinking suit produced by Darren Cross' abuse of Pym's shrinking technology.

216511.overview: Secrets of the Deep is a pinball table that released with the launch of Pinball FX2 as part of the Core Collection, and was re-released in all subsequent Pinball FX games. The table follows a crew of deep sea researchers, evading danger as they encounter shipwrecks full of priceless treasure on their quest to find the lost city of Atlantis.

460226.overview: Brazilian machine from 1981 with a playfield-design based on Gottlieb's 1971 "Orbit" and art-design from Bally's "Space Invaders".

461840.overview:
Al Capone pinball was released in 1983 (with some sources citing 1984) by the Brazilian manufacturer LTD do Brasil. It is a solid-state table themed around the famous American gangster and 1930s prohibition-era motifs. The table is a clone of Bally's 1982 machine, Speakeasy.

The game features two flippers, three pop bumpers, two slingshots, two kick-out holes, a five-bank of flyaway targets, a spinning target, a standup target, left and right crossover return lanes, and a roulette wheel in the playfield.

461847.overview:
Arizona is a solid-state electronic pinball machine released in December 1977 by LTD do Brasil, a prominent manufacturer based in Campinas, São Paulo. Designed for up to two players, the game adopts a classic American West frontier theme. Backglass artwork and promotional material suggest the full title may have been "Arizona Territory," reflecting the rugged cowboy motifs popular in arcade cabinets of that era.

The machine's playfield layout features elements typical of late-1970s Brazilian arcade engineering, including three banks of drop targets and unconventional inner lane guides near the flippers. Arizona operated as a standard replay table where successful scores could win players extra credits. It also included a classic match feature at the end of a game, awarding free credits for final scores ending in specific matching digits.

461861.overview: Amazon is a solid-state pinball machine released in 1979 by the Brazilian manufacturer LTD do Brasil. It is a notable entry from Brazil's peak pinball era.

464718.overview:
The goal of this table is to become an Adventure Land VIP through playing 4 mandatory multiball modes and completing 5 missions. Each multiball and mode has a different method of activation and different rules, described below.

Finishing all modes in a set of either multiballs or missions will light an extra ball.

468051.overview:
A pinball adaptation of the 2014 video game published by SEGA and set between the events of Alien and Aliens, this table follows Amanda Ripley in her harrowing efforts to stay one step ahead of a stalking Xenomorph aboard the space station Sevastopol.

This table was released as part of Zen Studio's Alien vs. Pinball mini collection. All three tables were available simultaneously on April 26, 2016, coinciding with what is known as "Alien Day" (due to the month and day numbers forming the code number of the colony where Aliens takes place in, LV-426) and marking the 30th anniversary of Aliens. 

The tables can be purchased separately as DLC in the games Zen Pinball 2, Pinball FX 2 and Pinball FX 3, as well as in the Zen Pinball mobile app.

The three tables are also free-to-play in the downloadable Aliens vs. Pinball mobile app. An Internet connection is required to play any of the three tables, and only Alien vs. Predator is available from the start. To unlock the other two tables, the player must complete three challenges each on the unlocked tables. Advertisements will play at the beginning of a new session, but they can be removed for a particular table (or for all tables), along with the need for online connectivity through an in-app purchase.

Since most Alien media involve graphic violence and strong language that would not be appropriate for children, Zen Studios has omitted such content from the pinball adaptations, allowing only milder swear words like "damn" and "bastard" and brief splashes of alien goo when Xenomorph eggs are destroyed in the Alien vs. Predator table. This allows the overall Everyone 10+ ESRB rating to be maintained across all Zen Pinball titles, but results in a higher Teen rating for the Android version of the Aliens vs. Pinball app, as well as a 12+ rating on the App Store for its iOS version.

468056.overview:
Recaptures the events of the highly-acclaimed 1986 film and sequel to Alien, where Ellen Ripley joins a squad of galactic marines to investigate a colony for Xenomorphs and are all drawn into a deadly struggle to eradicate them all.

This table was released as part of Zen Studio's Alien vs. Pinball mini collection. All three tables were available simultaneously on April 26, 2016, coinciding with what is known as "Alien Day" (due to the month and day numbers forming the code number of the colony where Aliens takes place in, LV-426) and marking the 30th anniversary of Aliens.

468057.overview:
Based on the premise and setting of the 2004 film directed by Paul W.S. Anderson, this table follows the journey of a young Predator who undergoes a rite of passage to become a seasoned warrior and Alien hunter within the bowels of a giant pyramid built in Antarctica and explored by Charles Bishop's expedition team in the film.

It was released as part of Zen Studio's Alien vs. Pinball mini collection. All three tables were available simultaneously on April 26, 2016, coinciding with what is known as "Alien Day" (due to the month and day numbers forming the code number of the colony where Aliens takes place in, LV-426) and marking the 30th anniversary of Aliens. 

The tables can be purchased separately as DLC in the games Zen Pinball 2, Pinball FX 2 and Pinball FX 3, as well as in the Zen Pinball mobile app.

468536.overview:
The Avengers is one of the four Marvel pinball tables that are part of the Avengers Chronicles Pack, released in 2012 and available for Zen Pinball 2, Pinball FX 2 and Pinball FX 3. Based on the blockbuster film The Avengers, this table involves uniting various Marvel superheroes under the leadership of SHIELD director Nick Fury to confront Loki and thwart his scheme to rule the world with an alien army.

Months after this table was released, Stern produced a physical pinball adaptation of the film with different designs, mechanics and behaviors than Zen's The Avengers table.

468588.overview: A-Force is one of the two Marvel pinball tables that are part of the Women of Power pack, released in the fall of 2016 and available for Zen Pinball 2, Pinball FX 2 and Pinball FX 3. Based on the 2015 comic book series of the same title, this table covers an original story in which Black Widow and Madame Masque accidentally end up in a different reality where the Soviet Union takes over the United States after a fight that destroys the Cosmic Cube. The two unlikely partners must put aside their differences to restore reality.

468669.overview:
Find the real meaning of Christmas in A Charlie Brown Christmas Pinball! Join the Peanuts crew in putting on a play and decorating the most perfect tree there is.

Table features:

- Snowflakes fall on the playfield, shoot the ball to eat them before they melt
- Feed Snoopy a snack by shooting his bowl
- Choose the perfect Christmas tree by shooting the right lanes
- Decorate Snoopy's house in Multiball to win the Lights and Display contest
- Direct the play in the Wizard mode and bring the Peanuts crew together to celebrate!

468685.overview:
Take on the Hyakki bandit clan to avenge your fallen Master! Train yourself in various fields to take on their leader, Maou in the final showdown.

Designed by Zoltan Hegyi, this table was released for Pinball FX as part of the Honor and Legacy Pack in 2023.

470400.overview: Unlicensed homebrew pinball table for Visual Pinball X based on the 1980s American TV show.

470680.overview: A homebrew mod of Bally's 1989 table "Mousin' Around!" for Visual Pinball X themed around American cars, tattoos and pin-ups.

470684.overview:
Amy Winehouse (14 September 1983 – 23 July 2011) was a British singer, songwriter, musician, and businesswoman. She is known for her distinctive contralto vocals, expressive and autobiographical songwriting, and eclectic blend of genres such as soul, rhythm and blues, and jazz. Her music, along with her fashion and highly publicised personal life, made her an influential figure in popular culture.

This homebrew table was released for Visual Pinball X in 2025.

470694.overview: Homebrew table for Visual Pinball X based on Nintendo's popular villiage-living social simulator.

472088.overview:
An original table for Future Pinball based on Wes Craven's supernatural slasher franchise. Although Gottlieb did release a "Freddy: A Nightmare On Elm Street" physical table in 1994, this release by SLAMT1LT has very little in common with that table, and is a superior experience, with better artwork, a more interesting table layout, video clips from the movie, and more satisfying gameplay and features.

A mod with support for FizX3 physics was released by HZR in 2023.

472343.overview: Built from the ground up for Visual Pinball X, this table eschews the modern style and MCU-themed artwork of Stern's 2012 table, and instead embraces a classic comic book look and feel.

472513.overview: An underwater-themed solid state table released in 1978 by Brazilian manufacturer, LTD do Brasil.

472689.overview: Boasting possibly the widest selection of music of any video game ever created, no unfair ball drains, and plenty of clips from the TV show, Bigonia's American Dad pinball table for Visual Pinball X is a must-play for fans of Seth MacFarlane's animated adult sit-com.

472692.overview:
The Addams Family is the best-selling pinball table of all-time, so naturally there have been many digital recreations of it over the years, but one notable version is SLAMT1LT's ULTIMATE Pro Edition for Future Pinball. It makes many changes and enhancements, including:

 • A new Mansion Mode called "Classic Addams TV Show" that replaces the six-million point mode.
 • Video clips added
 • Revamped DMD graphics
 • Enhanced attract mode
 • New sideblades
 • New lighting
 • Switchable modes - choose from the original experience, sounds and music (retro) or an enhanced version with new sounds, music and features (modern). 

A revised version was released by GerorgeH in 2025 with improved physics and audio, a new black and white gameplay mode, and a color DMD.

473195.overview: Bally's electro-mechanical table from June 1976 gets the SLAMT1LT makeover treatment with the addition of a solid-state-era DMD, Middle-Eastern music and sound effects in keeping with the original table's theme, and extra lighting and effects.

473879.overview:
Abra Ca Dabra: ULTIMATE Edition is a modern overhaul of Popotte's Future Pinball recreation of Gottlieb’s ⁠1975 sorcery and magic-themed pinball machine. 

SLAMT1LT has applied his signature "ULTIMATE" formula to this version, adding modern-style lighting and music, more advanced ball physics, and even providing the voice for the magician, to create a fun arcade version of this classic electro-mechanical table.

474131.overview: Released for Visual Pinball 9 the same year as Stern released their physical AC/DC pinball machine, nonetheless this is an original table that is a completely different game to Stern's. It was later ported to Visual Pinball X in 2020 by Goldchicco.

474179.overview: AC/DC: ULTIMATE Edition for Future Pinball is based on Stern's AC/DC table, but with new artwork, new features and improvements, and all studio tracks replaced with live versions.

474263.overview: D Struct's recreation of Stern's 1980 table "Ali" receives a mod from NitroNimbus which improves the physics, but also adds audio callouts and music inspired by the man widely regarded as the greatest boxer of all time, Muhammad Ali.

480015.overview: Released as a tribute to one of the best-selling music groups of all time, Gray Ghost's ABBA table for Visual Pinball X is a mod of Vortex (Taito do Brasil, 1981).

480042.overview:
Adventure is an original Visual Pinball table created by Eala Dubh (aka Dave Sanders), from an idea by Christopher Bair. It is based on the early action-adventure video game that was released for the Atari 2600 in 1980.

The build of the table is influenced by the Atari widebody games of the late 1970s. Music has been taken from Legend Of Valkyrie (Namco, 1989), with sounds 'borrowed' from Black Knight (1980), and other Williams arcade games.

The table has a "Sword Power" feature that can be activated with the left and right control keys. It is a two-second ball saver that blocks off the drain and outlanes. It starts the game lit, and once activated cannot be reused until lit again.

480178.overview: Released for Visual Pinball X by Donuts, the table keeps the table layout, rom file, DMD and sounds from "Attack From Mars" (Bally/Midway, 1995), but gives a visual reskin based on the "Mars Attacks!" movie from 1996. An optional PuP pack was also released, providing video clips from the movie.

480264.overview:
They're juicy, they're angry, and they're coming for your high score!

Attack of the Killer Tomatoes is a mod of Seawitch (Stern, 1980) for Visual Pinball X and is based on a 1978 independent movie.

480632.overview:
In the original "Alien" movie from 1979, the USCSS Nostromo is the name of Weyland-Yutani Corporation's ship that Ripley and the other members of the seven-man crew are returning to Earth on. 

Alien Nostromo for Visual Pinball X is a mod of Delta23's Aliens table (version 2.0).

480633.overview:
Released for Visual Pinball X in 2024, Alien Nostromo 2 is a mod of Gh0stbust3r's Alien Nostromo table, which was a mod of Delta23's Aliens table, which was a mod of JP Salas' recreation of Sorcerer (Williams, 1985).

This table adds new artwork and new sound effects to the familiar playfield layout and theme.

480637.overview: Inspired by the 2011 Nintendo DS video game "Alien Infestation", and the whole Alien franchise more generally, this Future Pinball table was released by Jipar in March 2013, and is a mod of Roney Pinball's "Thundercats" table.

480638.overview:
Despite continuing to develop tables for Future Pinball, and showcasing them on his YouTube channel, Aliens: Legendary Edition is the first public release of a table by SLAMT1LT for over four years. Released exclusively via his YouTube channel in a seemingly doomed attempt to reach 10,000 subscribers, Aliens: Legendary Edition is SLAMT1LT's latest version of the Aliens Legacy table originally created by David Eisner in 2010. 

The primary hook of the table's gameplay revolves around raw survival, closely mimicking the high-tension pacing of the movies. Players must constantly monitor an active Motion Tracker displayed on the playfield to track an approaching swarm of Xenomorphs. If the player fails to prioritize and eliminate threats by making accurate skill shots into specific areas, like the pop bumpers, the aliens will breach the defensive perimeter, immediately disabling the flippers and ending the ball. This mechanic turns traditional pinball score-chasing into a frantic battle against an active, aggressive enemy AI.

Visually, the Legendary Edition stands as a showcase for what is achievable with Future Pinball when paired with BAM (Better Arcade Mode). The layout boasts completely redesigned apron art, dynamic illumination options, and remarkably detailed animated models, including a responsive Ellen Ripley and custom alien egg pod bumpers. When significant milestones are achieved or when a power cut occurs on the table, the lighting transitions seamlessly to mirror the cold, terrifying atmosphere of the films.

Under the hood, the modern physics engine ensures that the ball behavior feels heavy and accurate, and combined with the high-fidelity sound effects, music and classic movie callouts that play throughout the experience, the result is an incredibly immersive and atmospheric tribute to the iconic sci-fi horror franchise.

480717.overview:
A renegade pilot, Stringfellow Hawke and his partner Dominic Santini, "steal" an advanced battle helicopter that they feel would be used unethically by its owners, a secretive U.S. intelligence agency. They agree to continue flying it on missions for the agency in exchange for the agency's help locating the pilot's missing brother. Use your pinball skills to help the Airwolf team complete their missions!

Released for Visual Pinball X in 2020, Airwolf is a re-theme of Cosmic (Taito do Brasil, 1980) based on the American action military drama television series that was created by Donald P. Bellisario and ran for four seasons, from January 22, 1984, until August 7, 1987.

481036.overview: Inspired by the live-action & CGI Alvin and the Chipmunks movies released between 2007-2015, Phenom's table is a re-theme of Skateball (Bally, 1980) for Visual Pinball X.

482144.overview: The layout of Apache! (Taito do Brasil, 1978) is identical to Fast Draw (Gottlieb, 1975), but instead of a cowboy theme, the artwork is focused on Native Americans. This recreation of Apache! for Future Pinball adds Native American-influenced audio callouts and the famous instrumental track "Apache!" by The Shadows during gameplay.
